subject: Materials Science
title: Nanoparticles in Energy Storage
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nanoparticles in Energy Storage usable.

hook.text: Nano-sized electrode materials charge batteries in minutes, not hours — short diffusion paths speed everything up.

buildup.text: Lithium ions diffuse through electrode particles — smaller means shorter paths and faster charging.

discovery.text: Nano-LiFePO₄ enabled fast-charging lithium batteries — bulk LiFePO₄ was too slow until nanostructuring solved it.

twist.text: Nanoparticles have low packing density — more surface means more side reactions with electrolyte, cutting battery life.

climax.text: Silicon nanowires expand 300% during lithiation without cracking — unlocking 10x the capacity of graphite anodes.

punchline.text: Shrink the electrode, charge faster — but nanoscale trade-offs remain.

quiz.question: Why do nanostructured electrodes charge faster?
options: Shorter diffusion distances allow lithium ions to move in and out more quickly
